title: Shemirat Halashon 33

chapters.title: The prohibition of Rechilut
chapters.about: Defining Rechilut and why it is forbidden even if true

chapters.title: Confronting the subject
chapters.about: Why it is forbidden to tell someone they were spoken about

chapters.title: Creating animosity
chapters.about: How gossip leads to hatred between people

chapters.title: Intentions and Teshuvah
chapters.about: How to fix the sin of Rechilut through Teshuvah

chapters.title: Listening to gossip
chapters.about: The prohibition of accepting or believing Rechilut

summary: Rabbi Soffer explains the laws of Rechilut, or gossip, as outlined in the Chafetz Chaim. He discusses why it is forbidden to speak or listen to gossip even if it is true, and how one can perform Teshuvah if they have already transgressed these laws.
questions: Is it forbidden to speak gossip if what I am saying is completely true?
Am I allowed to tell someone that another person spoke negatively about them?
What should I do if I have already committed the sin of Rechilut?
Is it forbidden to listen to gossip even if I do not believe it?
Why is the person who accepts gossip considered worse than the person who speaks it?
